problems.constraints:
- `1 <= points.length <= 500`
- `0 <= x, y <= 4 * 10^4`; all points distinct
problems.statement:
Given distinct points in the plane, return the minimum area of a rectangle with sides parallel to the axes whose four corners are all among the
points, or `0` if no such rectangle exists.
problems.title: Minimum Area Rectangle

problems.constraints:
- `1 <= points.length <= 10`
- `0 <= x, y <= 100`; all points distinct
problems.statement:
Choose four of the given points as the corners of a rectangle with sides parallel to the axes, such that **no other point** lies inside the
rectangle or on its border. Return the largest possible area, or `-1` if no such rectangle exists.
problems.title: Maximum Area Rectangle With Point Constraints I

problems.statement:
Reverse the decimal digits of the signed 32-bit integer `x` (keeping its sign). If the result falls outside the signed 32-bit range
`[-2^31, 2^31 - 1]`, return `0`. Assume you can't store 64-bit integers.
problems.title: Reverse Integer

problems.constraints:
- `1 <= points.length <= 10`
- `-100 <= x, y <= 100`; all points distinct
problems.statement: Return the minimum number of straight lines needed so that every one of the given distinct points lies on at least one line.
problems.title: Minimum Number of Lines to Cover Points

tests.explanation: One line through the first three, one through [4,3].

problems.statement:
Remove exactly one point from `points`, then take the maximum Manhattan distance (`|x1 - x2| + |y1 - y2|`) between any two remaining points.
Return the smallest possible value of that maximum.
problems.title: Minimize Manhattan Distances

problems.constraints:
- `3 <= points.length <= 10^4`
- `-10^4 <= x, y <= 10^4`; the polygon is simple
problems.statement:
`points` lists the vertices of a simple polygon (its edges don't cross each other) in order, either clockwise or counter-clockwise. Return `true`
if the polygon is convex. Consecutive collinear vertices are allowed.
problems.title: Convex Polygon

problems.constraints:
- `2 <= coordinates.length <= 1000`
- `-10^4 <= x, y <= 10^4`; all points distinct
problems.statement: `coordinates` holds distinct points. Return `true` if all of them lie on one straight line.
problems.title: Check If It Is a Straight Line

problems.statement:
A *valid cut* on a circle is either a straight segment through the centre touching the edge at two points, or a segment from the centre to one
point on the edge. Return the minimum number of valid cuts needed to divide the circle into `n` equal slices.
problems.title: Minimum Cuts to Divide a Circle

problems.statement:
Given four points in any order, return `true` if they are the vertices of a square (four equal positive sides and four right angles; the
square may be rotated).
problems.title: Valid Square

problems.constraints: - `-10^9 <= coordinates <= 10^9`; each rectangle has positive area
problems.statement:
An axis-aligned rectangle is given as `[x1, y1, x2, y2]` (bottom-left and top-right corners, with positive width and height). Return `true` if
the two rectangles overlap with **positive area**; touching edges or corners don't count.
problems.title: Rectangle Overlap

problems.statement:
Visit the points in the given order. In one second you can move one unit vertically, one unit horizontally, or one unit diagonally (both at
once). Return the minimum number of seconds.
problems.title: Minimum Time Visiting All Points

problems.constraints:
- `-10^4 <= all coordinates <= 10^4`
- `ax1 <= ax2`, `ay1 <= ay2`, `bx1 <= bx2`, `by1 <= by2`
problems.statement:
Two axis-aligned rectangles are given by their bottom-left and top-right corners: `(ax1, ay1)-(ax2, ay2)` and `(bx1, by1)-(bx2, by2)`. Return the
total area covered by the two rectangles (overlapping area is counted once).
problems.title: Rectangle Area

problems.statement:
For each query `[cx, cy, r]`, count the points of `points` that lie inside the circle of radius `r` centred at `(cx, cy)`; points exactly on the
circle count as inside. Return the counts.
problems.title: Queries on Number of Points Inside a Circle

problems.constraints:
- `1 <= points.length <= 300`
- `-10^4 <= x, y <= 10^4`; all points distinct
problems.statement: Given distinct points in the plane, return the maximum number of them that lie on one straight line.
problems.title: Max Points on a Line

problems.statement:
You stand at `location` and can turn to face any direction; you see every point within an angle of `angle` degrees (inclusive at both edges)
around your facing direction. Points exactly at your location are always visible, and points never block each other. Return the maximum number of
points you can see at once.
problems.title: Maximum Number of Visible Points

problems.statement:
`bombs[i] = [x, y, r]` is a bomb at `(x, y)` with blast radius `r`. When a bomb explodes it detonates every bomb whose centre is within distance
`r` (inclusive), which may trigger further explosions. You may detonate exactly one bomb by hand. Return the maximum number of bombs that can
end up exploding.
problems.title: Detonate the Maximum Bombs

tests.explanation: The second bomb reaches the first but not the other way round.

problems.statement:
Starting at `(0, 0)`, move `distance[0]` units north, then `distance[1]` west, `distance[2]` south, `distance[3]` east, and keep turning
counter-clockwise. Return `true` if the path ever crosses or touches itself.
problems.title: Self Crossing

problems.constraints:
- `1 <= trees.length <= 3000`
- `0 <= x, y <= 100`; all positions distinct
problems.statement:
`trees[i] = [x, y]` is the position of a tree (all positions distinct). Fence the whole garden with the shortest possible rope: the fence is the
convex hull of the trees. Return every tree lying **on** the fence (including trees in the middle of a straight fence segment), in any order.
problems.title: Erect the Fence

tests.explanation: Collinear trees are all on the fence.

problems.statement: A positive integer is *magical* if it is divisible by `a` or by `b`. Return the `n`-th magical number, modulo `10^9 + 7`.
problems.title: Nth Magical Number

problems.statement:
`num1` and `num2` are non-negative integers written as decimal strings (no leading zeros except for `"0"`). Return their sum as a string, without
converting the inputs to integers directly or using big-integer libraries.
problems.title: Add Strings

problems.statement: Return the least number of perfect squares (`1, 4, 9, 16, ...`) that add up to `n`.
problems.title: Perfect Squares

problems.statement:
Return `true` if the integer `x` reads the same forwards and backwards in decimal (a minus sign breaks the symmetry). Try it without converting
`x` to a string.
problems.title: Palindrome Number

problems.statement: The Fibonacci numbers are `F(0) = 0`, `F(1) = 1` and `F(n) = F(n - 1) + F(n - 2)`. Return `F(n)`.
problems.title: Fibonacci Number

problems.statement:
Write the non-negative integer `num` in English words, capitalising each word (for example `12345` is `"Twelve Thousand Three Hundred Forty
Five"`). Use single spaces, no `"and"` and no hyphens.
problems.title: Integer to English Words

tests.expected: Twelve Thousand Three Hundred Forty Five
One Million Two Hundred Thirty Four Thousand Five Hundred Sixty Seven
Two Billion One Hundred Forty Seven Million Four Hundred Eighty Three Thousand Six Hundred Forty Seven
One Billion Three Hundred Thirty Three Million Five Hundred Eighty One Thousand Nine
One Hundred Eighty Seven Million Two Hundred Seven Thousand Nine Hundred Nineteen

problems.constraints:
- `1 <= number of nodes in each list <= 100`
- `0 <= Node.val <= 9`
problems.statement:
Two non-negative integers are stored in linked lists with their digits in **reverse** order (the head is the ones digit), one digit per node and
no leading zeros except for the number `0` itself. Return their sum as a linked list in the same format.
problems.title: Add Two Numbers

problems.statement:
`digits` is a non-negative integer written as its decimal digits, most significant first, without leading zeros. Add one to it and return the
resulting digits.
problems.title: Plus One

problems.statement:
Rotating a digit by 180 degrees turns `0, 1, 6, 8, 9` into `0, 1, 9, 8, 6`; the digits `2, 3, 4, 5, 7` become invalid. A *confusing number*
becomes a **different** valid number when rotated as a whole (leading zeros of the result are ignored). Return `true` if `n` is confusing.
problems.title: Confusing Number

problems.statement:
There is a heap of `n` stones. You and a friend alternate turns, you first; each turn removes 1, 2 or 3 stones, and whoever removes the last stone
wins. Both players play optimally. Return `true` if you can win.
problems.title: Nim Game

tests.explanation: Whatever you take, your friend takes the rest.

problems.statement:
`n` bulbs start off. In round 1 you turn every bulb on; in round 2 you toggle every second bulb; in round `i` you toggle every `i`-th bulb; you
finish after round `n`. Return how many bulbs are on at the end.
problems.title: Bulb Switcher

problems.statement:
You have two jugs holding `x` and `y` litres and an unlimited water supply. You may fill a jug completely, empty a jug, or pour one jug into the
other until the receiving jug is full or the pouring jug is empty. Return `true` if you can end up with exactly `target` litres in total across
both jugs.
problems.title: Water and Jug Problem

problems.statement:
Exactly one of `buckets` buckets holds poison. A pig that drinks poison dies after `minutesToDie` minutes. In each round you may make any pigs
drink from any buckets simultaneously and then wait `minutesToDie` minutes; you have `minutesToTest` minutes in total. Return the minimum number
of pigs that guarantees identifying the poisoned bucket.
problems.title: Poor Pigs

problems.statement: `num` is the array form of a non-negative integer (its digits from left to right, no leading zeros). Return the array form of `num + k`.
problems.title: Add to Array-Form of Integer

problems.statement:
String `t` *divides* string `s` if `s` is `t` repeated one or more times. Return the longest string that divides both `str1` and `str2`, or `""`
if there is none.
problems.title: Greatest Common Divisor of Strings

problems.statement: Return the number of non-empty substrings of `s` that contain a single distinct letter (substrings at different positions count separately).
problems.title: Count Substrings with Only One Distinct Letter

tests.explanation: aaa: 1, aa: 2, a: 4, b: 1 — 8 in all.

problems.constraints: - each string is a valid representation as described above
problems.statement:
`s` and `t` are non-negative rational numbers written with an optional repeating part in parentheses: `"12"`, `"0.5"`, `"1."`, `"2.12"` and
`"0.1(6)"` are all valid (`"0.1(6)"` means `0.1666...`). The integer part has at most 4 digits, the non-repeating decimals at most 4, and the
repeating part at most 4. Return `true` if `s` and `t` denote the same number.
problems.title: Equal Rational Numbers

problems.statement:
A number in base `-2` is given as its bits from most to least significant: `[1, 1, 0, 1]` means `(-2)^3 + (-2)^2 + (-2)^0 = -3`. Both inputs have
no leading zeros (except for `[0]`). Return their sum in the same format, without leading zeros.
problems.title: Adding Two Negabinary Numbers

problems.statement: Return `true` if `n` equals `3^x` for some integer `x >= 0`. Try to solve it without loops or recursion.
problems.title: Power of Three

problems.statement: Return the base-7 representation of the integer `num` as a string (with a leading `-` for negative numbers).
problems.title: Base 7

problems.statement:
A *k-mirror number* is a positive integer with no leading zeros that reads the same forwards and backwards in **both** base 10 and base `k` (for
example `9` is 2-mirror: `9` in base 10 and `1001` in base 2). Return the sum of the `n` smallest k-mirror numbers.
problems.title: Sum of k-Mirror Numbers

problems.statement:
`nums` is 1-indexed and has length `n`. Element `nums[i]` is *special* if `i` divides `n`. Return the sum of the squares of all special
elements.
problems.title: Sum of Squares of Special Elements

problems.statement:
Repeatedly replace `num` with the sum of its decimal digits until it has a single digit, and return that digit. Try an `O(1)` solution without
loops.
problems.title: Add Digits

problems.statement: Return the number of prime numbers strictly less than `n`.
problems.title: Count Primes

problems.statement: Compute `x` raised to the power `n` (`x^n`) without a built-in power function. Answers within `10^-5` are accepted.
problems.title: Pow(x, n)

problems.statement:
`n` friends numbered `1` to `n` sit in a circle. Starting from friend 1, count `k` friends clockwise (including the one you start from); the
friend counted last leaves the circle, and counting restarts from the next friend clockwise. The last friend remaining wins; return their number.
problems.title: Find the Winner of the Circular Game

problems.statement: `nums` is a permutation of `0..n-1`. Return `ans` with `ans[i] = nums[nums[i]]`. As a follow-up, try doing it in place with `O(1)` extra space.
problems.title: Build Array from Permutation

problems.constraints:
- `1 <= columnTitle.length <= 7`, uppercase letters
- the answer is at most `2^31 - 1` (the largest title is `"FXSHRXW"`)
problems.statement: Spreadsheet columns are titled `A, B, ..., Z, AA, AB, ..., AZ, BA, ...`. Given a column title, return its column number (`A` is 1).
problems.title: Excel Sheet Column Number

problems.statement: List the positive factors of `n` in ascending order and return the `k`-th one, or `-1` if `n` has fewer than `k` factors.
problems.title: The kth Factor of n

problems.statement:
A *perfect number* equals the sum of its positive divisors excluding itself (for example `28 = 1 + 2 + 4 + 7 + 14`). Return `true` if `num` is
perfect.
problems.title: Perfect Number
